> Owner choice before STEWARD2 starts: under the steward every session belongs to a principal, so the UART console session must be someone's. Options: a manifest field names the principal (recommended: `"console": "alice"`, a Console row in the core, the bench's shell boots keep working through the steward); no console session in M1 (SSH only; the shell's console cases move to SSH and run alone); the console as approve@box only. ### Architect · Owner decision requested

Event: `fc549e2c3f0504a9d0dd471889e5b61d` · 2026-10-06T01:41:45Z

> The steward: whose session is the UART console?
> 
> 1. Today init starts the shell on the UART console directly, as a manifest server with no principal. Under the steward every session belongs to a principal and is carved from that principal's sub-budget. Whose session should the physical console be, in M1? The pages call the physical console a trusted path (M5 enrols the first owner there) and leave the M1 case unstated.
>    - A manifest field names the principal (recommended): Recommended. `"console": "alice"` in the boot manifest: at boot the steward opens that principal's unlabelled session on the UART and reopens it when it ends. The core gains one row (Console, no key). The bench's shell boots keep working through the steward, and the console's authority is a named principal's, visible in the manifest. Physical access already equals owning the box (the tenets).
>    - No console session in M1: Sessions exist only over SSH; the UART shows init's and the servers' lines only. The bench's shell cases (userland-boot and the shell's console cases) move to SSH sessions, which run alone under the shared-host rule and cost a login each. Nothing is granted to whoever holds the cable.
>    - The console is an approval channel only: The UART serves approve@box (the trusted path for approvals, as M5's enrolment console) and no shell. Approvals need no SSH, but the shell has no console boot until SSH sessions work, and STEWARD3's approve@box over sshd is still needed for remote use.
